content:
Recently I was modulizing the Formal Conjectures repo and ran into issues; namely the repo uses native_decide quite a bit and many proofs using native_decide suddenly broke.

To provide a #MWE:

Suppose we have File A and File B, with File A being:

module

public def importedValue : Nat :=
  [40, 2].foldl Nat.add 0

and file B:

module

import A

example : importedValue = 42 := by
  native_decide

Then building file A works, but file B does not, with the following error message

Error message

error: B.lean:6:2: Tactic native_decide failed: Could not evaluate decidable instance. Error: (interpreter) IR of declaration 'importedValue' not available; this may point to a missing meta check in a metaprogram
error: Lean exited with code 1
Some required targets logged failures:
- B
error: build failed

Adding the meta keyword to the import fixes this, as well as removing the module keyword in file B.

However, what is the most confusing: This issue is not visible in the VSCode preview, it only appears when doing lake build (or lake env).

Is this a known issue (for the VSCode extension?)?
Yesn't: Just adding expose to the def doesnt work, but when the value is exposed we can first unfold and then native_decide, which works

I'm honestly not surprised it doesn't appear in the language server, the language imports more things than just the build, including code for all imported declarations for convenient #eval but meta import is the right thing to do here.
This reminds of #verso > Custom command works in VS Code, fails under lake build @ 💬, which mentions differences in the module system between the LSP and lake build
The same thing happens with #eval: #eval in the language server can do more than in a lake build.
For #eval this is genuinely intended as in the vast cases, it is used as a temporary command anyway, but for native_decide this is likely the wrong behavior (and error message), yes!
